title: Repository performance profiling governance
purpose: Consolidate measured baseline timing, memory, bottleneck, incremental-validation, and safe-parallelisation guidance for repository optimisation work without changing implementation behaviour or weakening validation gates.

coveredIssues.title: Performance bottleneck profiling
coveredIssues.completionBasis: USF-384 supplied profiled command timings, slowest-command ranking, failures, peak memory observations, artifact observations, and assurance impact. This artefact consolidates candidate fixes and the required no-regression posture.

coveredIssues.title: Validator bottleneck profiling
coveredIssues.completionBasis: USF-384 identified validator-heavy commands and slow aggregate validation behaviour. This artefact records bottlenecks and no-regression tests required before any optimisation.

coveredIssues.title: Incremental validation design
coveredIssues.completionBasis: This artefact defines input classes, hash strategy, cache key inputs, planted invalidation cases, and fail-closed fallback expectations.

coveredIssues.title: Safe parallelisation opportunities
coveredIssues.completionBasis: USF-385 supplied command critical-path analysis. This artefact records safe parallel tasks, unsafe serial tasks, shared resources, and a serial-versus-parallel validation plan.

coveredIssues.title: Memory usage profile
coveredIssues.completionBasis: USF-384 supplied per-command peak memory observations. This artefact records memory-heavy commands, risk, and safe optimisation candidates.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: IO hotspot profiling
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include declared-input inventories, one-pass reads, path-class manifests, large-tree exclusions, generated-output exclusion, and bytes-read measurement. Adoption requires coverage equivalence and fail-closed fallback on unknown inputs.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Duplicate JSON parse cost analysis
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include per-run parse reuse, catalogue and registry object reuse, schema-document reuse, content-addressed invalidation, and planted invalid JSON regression checks. Adoption requires strict parse behaviour to remain equivalent.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Glob and directory scan optimisation plan
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include manifest-first scanning, explicit path-class inventories, generated/evidence/cache exclusion, and affected-only directory walks. Adoption requires proof that no authority, validator, evidence, fixture, or command-surface input is omitted.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Large artifact scan avoidance
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include artifact manifests, retained-hash indexes, generated-report exclusion, evidence-retention class filters, and large-object path policies. Adoption must not hide raw evidence, accepted proof artifacts, or referenced generated reports.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Compose startup profiling
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include phase-split Compose timing, profile minimisation, warm-service reuse where safe, Testcontainers comparison, reset-cost measurement, healthcheck critical-path profiling, and service-specific isolation. Adoption requires provider-mode and environment equivalence.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Network dependency profiling
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include network-free defaults, dependency cache hit-rate measurement, provider-call labelling, local mirror/cache consideration, and explicit external-provider command classification. Adoption must not turn hermetic proof into live-provider proof.

realisedTimingOptionCoverage.title: Screenshot generation cost review
realisedTimingOptionCoverage.realisation: In scope for exhaustive timing evaluation. Candidate options include screenshot count and byte measurement, proof-only capture, deduplicated content-addressed capture, lazy report rendering, and browser-phase profiling. Adoption must preserve referenceability where screenshots are proof evidence.

baselineMeasurements.observation: missing from the root package script surface

coldCacheObservation.scope: isolated local clone with separate package store

slowestCommandRanking.command: proof-cockpit acceptance validation, lint, cold isolated install

bottleneckFindings.measurement: Timed out at 120 seconds with browser context closure error recorded by USF-384.
candidateFixes: Separate browser startup, navigation, screenshot, and assertion phases in future profiling.
Preserve timeout and failure evidence instead of converting timeout to pass.
Require before-and-after output comparison before reducing capture scope.
bottleneckFindings.assuranceImpact: Any optimisation must keep machine QA failures visible and must not convert timeout or unknown status into pass.

bottleneckFindings.measurement: 104 seconds, failed, about 317 MB peak memory.
candidateFixes: Use dependency-aware gating to avoid repeated work only when input hashes prove equivalence.
Split independent read-only validation phases only after serial-versus-parallel comparison passes.
Preserve aggregate failure ordering in generated summaries.
bottleneckFindings.assuranceImpact: Aggregate validation cannot be shortened by skipping required validators or hiding known failing gates.

bottleneckFindings.measurement: Enterprise validation 38 seconds, validate spec 32 seconds, validate spec selftest 13 seconds, all pass.
candidateFixes: Measure duplicate parse cost before adding shared parse cache.
Use content-addressed invalidation for semantic artefacts, catalogues, registries, schemas, and evidence.
Keep planted invalid and missing-input cases in validator selftests.
bottleneckFindings.assuranceImpact: Validator optimisation must remain fail-closed on invalid JSON, unknown controlled values, stale reports, and missing evidence.

bottleneckFindings.measurement: 12 seconds, failed, about 2.14 GB peak memory.
candidateFixes: Do not treat performance work as test repair.
Profile per-test memory only after current failure causes are tracked.
Avoid parallelising service-backed tests until port and fixture isolation are proven.
bottleneckFindings.assuranceImpact: Known failing tests remain evidence requirements and cannot be hidden by narrower command aliases.

validatorBottleneckNoRegressionTests.requiredBeforeOptimisation: Strict parse must still fail on invalid JSON and must still check taxonomy, vocabulary, and schema registry inputs.
Known bad schema states, unknown vocabulary values, missing evidence, stale reports, provider mismatch, and environment mismatch must remain failing cases.
Serial and optimised command paths must produce equivalent pass, fail, and evidence requirement classifications before any shortcut becomes default.
Generated report freshness must not satisfy proof claims without the underlying evidence.

memoryProfile.risk: Highest observed peak memory and currently failing.
safeOptimisationCandidates: Profile per-test memory after current failures are handled.
Avoid service-backed parallelism until isolation is proven.

memoryProfile.risk: Second-highest observed peak memory but passing.
safeOptimisationCandidates: Avoid changing type coverage to reduce memory.
Consider caching only after lockfile and source hash inputs are included.
Fix lint evidence requirements separately before performance claims.
Do not narrow lint scope without proving excluded paths are intentionally outside scope.

memoryProfile.risk: Long duration with moderate memory and known failure.
safeOptimisationCandidates: Deduplicate read-only validation phases only with content-addressed invalidation.
Keep aggregate failure status and evidence requirement visibility.
Separate acceptance semantics from runtime proof evidence.
Do not allow human acceptance labels to imply final acceptance without authority.

hashStrategy.principle: Use content-addressed hashes over canonical input bytes plus canonical repository-relative path, not modification time alone.

plantedInvalidationCases: schema file missing when registry marks it active
invalid JSON introduced into a catalogue
generated report retained after source evidence changed
provider mode changed from hermetic-mock to live-external-provider
environment changed from production-shaped to production-live
incrementalValidationDesign.fallbackRule: Run the full relevant validation path when an input class, dependency, hash, provider mode, environment, evidence freshness marker, or generated report source cannot be resolved.

safeParallelTasks: independent strict JSON parse checks for separate catalogues after file discovery is complete
read-only documentation consistency scans that do not write shared reports
independent validator selftests that do not share mutable fixtures
report formatting after all source evidence has already been collected
non-overlapping artefact metadata inspection when no pruning or mutation occurs
unsafeSerialTasks: compose up, compose healthcheck, and compose down on shared loopback ports
tests that share service containers, seeded fixtures, or mutable evidence directories
validators that write to the same generated report path
proof-cockpit browser automation using shared browser context
any task whose output ordering is part of the evidence or audit trail
validationPlan: Run serial and parallel forms against the same input set.
Compare exit status, issue classification, generated report content, evidence references, and evidence requirement visibility.
Reject parallel execution if ordering, nondeterminism, or shared-resource contention changes the result.
Keep serial execution as the fallback on any ambiguity.

acceptanceCriteriaTrace.criterion: Report lists profiled commands, bottlenecks, measurements, and candidate fixes with assurance impact.
Profile report identifies top bottlenecks and no-regression tests needed before optimisation.
Design names input classes, hash strategy, cache key inputs, and planted invalidation cases.
Report lists safe parallel tasks, unsafe tasks, shared resources, and validation plan.
Report identifies memory-heavy commands, peak usage, risk, and safe optimisation candidates.

validationPlanForFutureOptimisation: Compare before-and-after command durations against USF-384 without hiding known failures.
Compare serial and parallel command outputs before enabling parallel defaults.
Keep full validation as the fallback whenever input resolution, cache state, evidence freshness, provider mode, or environment is unknown.
Require explicit evidence before claiming measured speedup for any timing option.
nonClaims: This artefact does not implement performance optimisation.
This artefact does not change validators, commands, package scripts, compose files, or runtime code.
This artefact does not make a readiness, staging, product, production, compliance, store, deployment, or release claim.
This artefact does not treat generated reports as semantic authority.
This artefact does not claim measured speedup for any timing option without before-and-after evidence.
